newsitem.title: USA: Hollywood readies for biggest night of year.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood readies for biggest night of year.

text.p: Thousands of movie fans braved the early morning chill in Los Angeles on Monday as Hollywood made last-minute preparations for it's biggest night of the year -- the Academy Awards gala.
Four 20-foot-tall (6.096-metres) replicas of the Oscar statue stood guard at the doors of the Shrine Auditorium to welcome the stars and the Hollywood power elite for the 69th annual Academy Awards.
Legions of fans, some of whom have been outside since Thursday, were armed with cameras to snap their favourites who were to stride along the red carpet later in the day.
"I slept on the concrete," Kenan Jones, who had camped out for two nights said. "It hurt bad, but it was worth it."
Other hardy fans had been camping in the temporary stands since they were erected on Thursday.

The Shrine Auditorium was a hub of activity early on Monday as carpenters hammered the final nails into the stage and scenery and electricians adjusted the 450 computer-controlled moving spotlights for the night when Hollywood outdoes itself with extravagance.

This is the night the movie-making capital of the world puts on a show. Part of the glitter will come from $140 million worth of diamonds donated by an international jeweller and destined for the necks, wrists and earlobes of the famous -- if only for Oscar night.
In addition, the world's most famous fashion designers have been knocking each other over to entice the stars to wear their gowns and tuxedos.
After the show, it's party time as studios hope to attract the rich and famous to their post-Oscar bashes.

Apart from the traditional "Governor's Ball" for 1,650 guests, Elton John's AIDS benefit party was expected to be the hottest ticket in town. The all-star guests will also have the chance to sing "Happy Birthday" to the singer, who turns 50 the following day.

This year, apart from Hollywood legend Lauren Bacall ("The Mirror Has Two Faces") in the best supporting actress category, there were no obvious favourites to grab the Oscars handed out by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

"The English Patient", which picked up the most nominations with 12, was thought to have a chance of winning for best picture, but is up against a Tom Cruise blockbuster, "Jerry Maguire" and three quirky independently produced films, "Secrets & Lies", "Shine" and "Fargo".
Lead actors, Ralph Fiennes and Kristin Scott Thomas and "The English Patient" director Anthony Minghella are nominated, along with Juliette Binoche, as best supporting actress.
Cruise and Fiennes are joined in the best actor category by Woody Harrelson for "The People vs. Larry Flynt", Geoffrey Rush for "Shine" and Billy Bob Thornton for "Sling Blade".
Along with Scott Thomas, the best actress nominees are Brenda Blethyn ("Secrets & Lies"), Frances McDormand ("Fargo"), Emily Watson ("Breaking the Waves") and Diane Keaton ("Marvin's Room").

James Woods is nominated for best supporting actor for "Ghosts of Mississippi", along with first-time nominees, Cuba Gooding Jr. ("Jerry Maguire"), William Macy ("Fargo"), Armin Mueller-Stahl ("Shine") and Edward Norton ("Primal Fear").
Besides Bacall and Binoche, supporting actresses are: Joan Allen ("The Crucible"), Barbara Hershey ("The Portrait of a Lady") and Marianne Jean-Baptiste ("Secrets & Lies").
Minghella is joined in the best director bracket by Joel Coen for "Fargo", Milos Forman for "The People vs. Larry Flynt", Scott Hicks for "Shine" and Mike Leigh for "Secrets & Lies."
The nominations for best foreign film are: "A Chef in Love" (Georgia), "Kolya" (Czech Republic), "The Other Side of Sunday" (Norway), "Prisoner of the Mountains" (Russia) and "Ridicule" (France).

The awards presentation, which begins at 9 p.m. EST (0200 GMT) is being broadcast live in the United States on ABC television and was expected to be seen by one billion viewers from about 100 countries worldwide. The show is scheduled to run for three hours, but in the past it has often gone longer.
